name: Handjass
description: Handjass, also known as Sackjass or Butzer, is considered the most basic and fundamental form of Jass, the national card game of Switzerland. It is a trick-taking game where players compete to reach a target score (usually represented by strokes on a slate) while avoiding the 'null' (potato) - a penalty for failing to reach a minimum point threshold in a hand.

content.text: Handjass, also known as Sackjass or Butzer, is considered the most basic and fundamental form of Jass, the national card game of Switzerland. It is a trick-taking game where players compete to reach a target score (usually represented by strokes on a slate) while avoiding the 'null' (potato) - a penalty for failing to reach a minimum point threshold in a hand.

Part of the extensive Jass family of games which have been popular in Switzerland since the late 18th century. Handjass is the 'direct' version of the game, simpler than the partnership-based Schieber.
36-card Jass deck (6-10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace). In German-speaking areas, the suits are Roses, Bells, Acorns and Shields. In French-speaking areas, standard French suits are used.
A slate or score sheet to mark 'strokes' (points).
Deal all cards (9 per player in a 4-player game). For 2-3 players, a 'blind hand' or 'besern' mechanic may be used.

items.text: Berner Handjass: Variation with different scoring multipliers for specific suits.
Different Point Thresholds: Some play with 21 point threshold instead of 26.
